clue.text: Dawn's endlessly conceited boast

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for conceited loses its final letter

parts.note: a cocky person is conceited
to crow is to boast

explanation.surface: Someone named Dawn is forever bragging about herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' docks the Y from COCKY. 'Dawn' looks like a woman's name but is the time of day; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cock crows at first light, so cockcrow is a traditional word for daybreak.

clue.text: Ruin cocoa when replanted around phosphorus mine

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go round the chemical symbol
replanted means the letters of ruin cocoa are set out again in a new order

parts.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A grower ruins a cocoa crop by replanting it around a phosphorus mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replanted' rearranges RUIN COCOA and 'around' puts that round P. 'mine' reads as a pit but means a rich source.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornucopia, the horn of plenty, is an abundant source, just as a mine of information is.

clue.text: Left to escape from jam in bar

indicators.note: to escape from means the letter for left gets out of the jam word

parts.note: to clog is to jam or block

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a pub crush is allowed to slip away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left to escape from' takes the L out of CLOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A cog is a projecting tooth or tenon, a short bar that engages another part.

clue.text: Girl from poly abandoning course in Canada

indicators.note: in means the shortened pudding goes inside the Canada letters
abandoning means the word poly is dropped from the pudding's name

parts.note: roly-poly is a pudding, a course of a meal

explanation.surface: A girl drops out of her polytechnic course to go to Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'course' is ROLY-POLY, a British jam sponge pudding; dropping POLY leaves ROLY, put inside CAN. 'poly' looks like a polytechnic.
explanation.definitionFit: Carolyn is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Divorced women maybe over time drink, it's long been believed

indicators.note: over means in this down clue the wives come above the rest

parts.note: ex-wives are old wives, former ones
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: Divorcees swap stories over a drink about beliefs held for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old wives' here means former wives, not elderly women.
explanation.definitionFit: An old wives' tale is a traditional belief, long accepted but unfounded.

clue.text: Branches revising rental

indicators.note: revising the word rental means reworking its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A landlord is reconsidering the rent charged across company branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revising' rearranges RENTAL. 'Branches' suggests company offices, but means the branching horns of a deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A deer's antler grows in tines that fork like the branches of a tree.

clue.text: Collapsed on ice after gaining a little weight over recent years

indicators.note: gaining means the rearranged letters take in the weight abbreviation
collapsed means the letters of on ice fall into a new order

parts.note: oz, an ounce, is a small weight

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed on the ice after putting on a little weight over recent years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collapsed' turns ON ICE into NEOIC and 'gaining' puts OZ inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neozoic is an old name for the recent era of geological time, the later ages of life.

clue.text: Stone circle over one's lounge incomplete, unlaid in odd places

parts.note: a lap is a circuit, a circle of a track
one is I, and the 's is is

indicators.note: incomplete means the lounging word loses its last letter

parts.note: to laze is to lounge

indicators.note: in odd places means taking the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of unlaid

explanation.surface: A stone circle lies beside a lounge left unfinished, its pavement unlaid in odd places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts LAZE to LAZ; 'in odd places' takes U, L, I from UNLAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapis lazuli is a deep blue semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Bank seldom taking a third off

indicators.note: taking a third off means removing two of the six letters of the word for seldom

parts.note: rarely means seldom

explanation.surface: A bank rarely cuts its fees by a third.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking a third off' removes RA, two of the six letters of RARELY. 'Bank' is a verb, as in bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on something is to rely on it, so here the verb means depend.

clue.text: Fashion business out of charity event swap

parts.note: a rag is a British student charity event, as in rag week
to trade is to swap

explanation.surface: A clothing firm comes out of a charity swap shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAG is a British student fundraising event, as in rag week.
explanation.definitionFit: The rag trade is an informal name for the clothing and fashion industry.

clue.text: Books in set including work about Saint

indicators.note: including means the set word holds the rest inside it

parts.note: jelly sets, or gels

indicators.note: about means the word for work goes around the saint's letter

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A boxed set of books contains a work about a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts OP round S to give OSP; 'including' puts that inside GEL. Three containers in a row are easy to get the wrong way round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospels are the first four books of the New Testament.

clue.text: People like you can have such influence!

definitions.text: People like you can have such influence!

parts.words: People like you can have such influence!
parts.note: people like you are your equals, and the clue describes the sway they hold over you

explanation.definitionFit: Peer pressure is the influence one's equals exert to make one conform.

clue.text: Like some plants, hesitate before redesigning fuel boilers

indicators.note: before means the hesitating word comes ahead of the rest

parts.note: um is the sound made when hesitating

indicators.note: redesigning the words fuel boilers means putting their letters in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An engineer pauses before redesigning a heating system's fuel-fed boilers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigning' turns FUEL BOILERS into BELLIFEROUS, which follows UM.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbelliferous plants, such as carrot and parsley, carry their flowers in umbrella-shaped clusters.

clue.text: Restriction placed on leg of 'green' commuter journey?

definitions.text: Restriction placed on leg of 'green' commuter journey?

parts.words: Restriction placed on leg of 'green' commuter journey?
parts.note: a cyclist commuting in an eco-friendly way fastens a band round one leg of their trousers

explanation.definitionFit: A cycle clip holds a trouser leg tight so it does not catch in the chain.

clue.text: Large pail's replaced sprinklers

indicators.note: replaced means the letters of large pail's are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A large bucket has been swapped for a set of garden sprinklers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges LARGE PAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspergilla are the brushes or perforated rods used to sprinkle holy water.

clue.text: Love to peruse old language

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis, the letter O
to scan a text is to peruse it

explanation.surface: A romantic enjoys poring over an ancient tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscan was an ancient Italic language of southern Italy, a relative of Latin.

clue.text: Leading centre backed bringing in university administrators

indicators.note: bringing in means the reversed pair takes the university letter inside
backed means both words are read from the end back to the start

parts.note: a star is a leading performer
the core is the centre

explanation.surface: A top research centre receives backing and recruits university administrators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns STARCORE into EROCRATS, and 'bringing in' adds U after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurocrats are the officials who run the European Union's institutions, administrators in Brussels.

clue.text: Suffer, receiving stick for cutting baby care facility

indicators.note: receiving means the word for suffer takes the rest inside it

parts.note: to incur a loss is to suffer it

indicators.note: for cutting means the stick word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a baton is a stick

explanation.surface: Someone takes a beating with a stick meant for cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cutting' trims BATON to BATO, which 'receiving' puts inside INCUR before its R.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubator is a heated enclosure where premature babies are cared for in hospital.

clue.text: Code for old military transport wasn't secret?

parts.note: a bus is a means of transport
hid O, hid nothing, is a cryptic way of saying nothing was kept secret

explanation.surface: Encrypted orders for an old army convoy were not kept confidential.
explanation.walkthrough: BUS HID O reads as 'the bus hid nothing', so the transport kept no secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushido was the code of honour of the samurai, Japan's old warrior class.

clue.text: He's first to protest at the vulgar?

definitions.text: He's first to protest at the vulgar?

indicators.note: first to means only the opening letter of protest is used

parts.note: rude means vulgar or coarse

explanation.surface: A man is quick to object whenever anything coarse appears.
explanation.walkthrough: P from 'first to protest' goes before RUDE, and the whole clue describes such a person too.
explanation.definitionFit: A prude is someone easily shocked by anything indecent, the first to complain about smut.

clue.text: Clown to go off stage first

indicators.note: first means the stage word comes ahead of the rest

parts.note: a pier is a landing stage
to rot is to go off, like food

explanation.surface: A clown is the opening act to leave the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: A landing stage is a PIER; 'first' puts it before ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the sad white-faced clown of French pantomime.

clue.text: Not demanding numbers for an audience

definitions.text: Not demanding numbers for an audience

parts.words: Not demanding numbers for an audience
parts.note: the clue describes songs that ask little effort of those who hear them

explanation.definitionFit: Easy listening is a genre of light, undemanding popular music.

clue.text: Impatient sound from one bothered by long words

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of contempt or impatience, like pah
A. A. Milne's bear calls himself a bear of very little brain whom long words bother

explanation.definitionFit: Pooh is an exclamation of disdain, and Winnie-the-Pooh says long words bother him.

clue.text: I would do well backing woman I love

indicators.note: backing means the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: a girl is a young woman
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A man declares he would thrive if he were going out with the woman he loves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses GIRL + I + O as a whole. 'do well' reads as 'thrive' but means drilling a well.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil rig drills wells, so it is something that does a well; a punning definition.

clue.text: Roman who runs in a line achieving his peak

parts.note: qui is the Latin word for who, as a Roman would say it
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Roman athlete running a straight course reaches his best form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' refers back to the Roman, so 'his peak' is a hill of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Quirinal is one of the seven hills of Rome, so a Roman's peak.

clue.text: Metal piece in locks drawn back up

indicators.note: up means in this down clue the hair word reads upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: locks of hair drawn back and pinned make a bun

explanation.surface: A metal part inside the locks is pulled back up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks drawn back' is BUN, hair pinned up; 'up' reverses it in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A nub is a small knob or lump, such as a stub of metal.

clue.text: Music bringing some cheer also source of bitterness

parts.note: hip is part of the cheer hip hip hooray
hops give beer its bitter taste

explanation.surface: A pub band brings good cheer along with bitter beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip-hop is a genre of popular music built on rap and beats.

clue.text: Green animal with no head and a little back

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry

indicators.note: with no head means the animal loses its first letter

parts.note: a zebra is an animal

explanation.surface: An inexperienced creature lacks a head and a proper spine.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is the heraldic word for green. 'with no head' drops the Z of ZEBRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertebra is one small bone of the spine, a little piece of the back.
